\chapter{Seven More Body Words, Spaced on Purpose}
\label{ch:ja-body-seven-more}
\hlchaptermodality{12}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read, write, hear, and say seven more body words while retrieving older script, greeting, farewell, and repair knowledge at expanding intervals.}

Seven fully decodable body labels interleaved with measured R3 and R4 retrieval rather than taught as a single topical list.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Retrieval 1 — mora, politeness, and \ja{し}}

\label{lesson:JA-R12-foundation-01}



\begin{quote}
Tap one mora for \textbf{\ja{い}}, then write \textbf{\ja{い}} and \textbf{\ja{し}} from memory. Hear, say, read, and write the first seven-word body map; finish by isolating \textbf{\ja{あし}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear a polite thank-you, say it, read \textbf{\ja{ありがとうございます}}, and choose it for someone outside your close circle.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one accurate card.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[atama]{\ja{あたま} — head}

\label{lesson:JA-C12-atama}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\ja{は}} and \textbf{\ja{日}}. Read \textbf{\ja{ございます}}, say \emph{yukkuri}, then retrieve \textbf{\ja{はな}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ja{あたま}} — \emph{a-ta-ma} — head
\end{quote}

Every sign is earned. Keep three even morae.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear, point, say, read, then hide and write \textbf{\ja{あたま}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://words.marugotoweb.jp/}{Japan Foundation Marugoto A1 vocabulary database}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kami]{\ja{かみ} — hair}

\label{lesson:JA-C12-kami}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\ja{あたま}}, read \textbf{\ja{はい}}, write \textbf{\ja{本}}, sketch the speech component, write \textbf{\ja{ゆ}}, and finish with \textbf{\ja{かお}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ja{かみ}} — \emph{ka-mi} — hair
\end{quote}

Two known signs, two morae.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear, point, say, read, then write \textbf{\ja{かみ}} from memory.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://words.marugotoweb.jp/}{Japan Foundation Marugoto A1 vocabulary database}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieval 2 — old signs, recent request}

\label{lesson:JA-R12-foundation-02}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\ja{え}} and \textbf{\ja{かみ}}. Build the five and mouth components of \textbf{\ja{語}}. Then ask someone to say it with \emph{itte kudasai} and write \textbf{\ja{め}}.

\section[ha]{\ja{は} — tooth}

\label{lesson:JA-C12-ha-tooth}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{\ja{はい}}, write \textbf{\ja{語}}, recall its Chinese-derived bridge, and write \textbf{\ja{もうすこし}}. Then hear, say, read, and write the first seven body words.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ja{は}} — \emph{ha} — tooth; teeth
\end{quote}

One sign is the complete word.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear, point, say, read, and write \textbf{\ja{は}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[kata]{\ja{かた} — shoulder}

\label{lesson:JA-C12-kata}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ja{かた}} — \emph{ka-ta} — shoulder
\end{quote}

Two known signs, two even morae.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear, point, say, read, then write \textbf{\ja{かた}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[senaka]{\ja{せなか} — back}

\label{lesson:JA-C12-senaka}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\ja{おなか}} and \textbf{\ja{に}}. Read \textbf{\ja{コーヒー}} as a katakana loan, then write small \textbf{\ja{っ}}.

\section[atama, kami, ha, kata, onaka, senaka …]{Seven more body words, spaced on purpose}

\label{lesson:JA-C12-body-map-two}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\ja{ありがとう}}. Then hear, say, read, and write any three words from the first seven-word body map.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ja{あたま・かみ・は・かた・おなか・せなか・こし}}
\end{quote}

Every sign is earned, and every new word has already had short and medium retrieval scheduled in this chapter.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Listen and point; say all seven; read all seven; then write any four from memory.
